case_title: Khuman Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act s.3(2)(v)
aggravating_circumstances: Calling the deceased by his caste name, use of axe, infliction of head injuries
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC and s.3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act, sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The accused and the victim were involved in a dispute over grazing rights. The accused arrived at the victim's field with his buffaloes, and the victim objected, leading to a verbal altercation. The accused then struck the victim on the head with an axe, causing six head injuries. The victim fell and later died from the injuries. The prosecution presented eyewitness accounts and a medical report indicating the cause of death was due to excessive bleeding. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC and the SC/ST Act, while the High Court affirmed the conviction. The Supreme Court, however, found that the incident occurred in a sudden fight without premeditation, thus modifying the conviction to Section 304 Part II IPC. The conviction under the SC/ST Act was set aside as there was no evidence the offense was committed solely because the victim was a member of a Scheduled Caste.
